51: /// A queue of delayed elements.
52: ///
53: /// Once an element is inserted into the `DelayQueue`, it is yielded once the
54: /// specified deadline has been reached.
55: ///
56: /// # Usage
57: ///
58: /// Elements are inserted into `DelayQueue` using the [`insert`] or
59: /// [`insert_at`] methods. A deadline is provided with the item and a [`Key`] is
60: /// returned. The key is used to remove the entry or to change the deadline at
61: /// which it should be yielded back.
62: ///
63: /// Once delays have been configured, the `DelayQueue` is used via its
64: /// [`Stream`] implementation. [`poll_expired`] is called. If an entry has reached its
65: /// deadline, it is returned. If not, `Poll::Pending` is returned indicating that the
66: /// current task will be notified once the deadline has been reached.
67: ///
68: /// # `Stream` implementation
69: ///
70: /// Items are retrieved from the queue via [`DelayQueue::poll_expired`]. If no delays have
71: /// expired, no items are returned. In this case, `Poll::Pending` is returned and the
72: /// current task is registered to be notified once the next item's delay has
73: /// expired.
74: ///
75: /// If no items are in the queue, i.e. `is_empty()` returns `true`, then `poll`
76: /// returns `Poll::Ready(None)`. This indicates that the stream has reached an end.
77: /// However, if a new item is inserted *after*, `poll` will once again start
78: /// returning items or `Poll::Pending`.
79: ///
80: /// Items are returned ordered by their expirations. Items that are configured
81: /// to expire first will be returned first. There are no ordering guarantees
82: /// for items configured to expire at the same instant. Also note that delays are
83: /// rounded to the closest millisecond.
84: ///
85: /// # Implementation
86: ///
87: /// The [`DelayQueue`] is backed by a separate instance of a timer wheel similar to that used internally
88: /// by Tokio's standalone timer utilities such as [`sleep`]. Because of this, it offers the same
89: /// performance and scalability benefits.
90: ///
91: /// State associated with each entry is stored in a [`slab`]. This amortizes the cost of allocation,
92: /// and allows reuse of the memory allocated for expired entries.
93: ///
94: /// Capacity can be checked using [`capacity`] and allocated preemptively by using
95: /// the [`reserve`] method.
96: ///
97: /// # Usage
98: ///
99: /// Using `DelayQueue` to manage cache entries.
100: ///
101: /// ```rust,no_run
102: /// use tokio_util::time::{DelayQueue, delay_queue};
103: ///
104: /// use futures::ready;
105: /// use std::collections::HashMap;
106: /// use std::task::{Context, Poll};
107: /// use std::time::Duration;
108: /// # type CacheKey = String;
109: /// # type Value = String;
110: ///
111: /// struct Cache {
112: ///     entries: HashMap<CacheKey, (Value, delay_queue::Key)>,
113: ///     expirations: DelayQueue<CacheKey>,
114: /// }
115: ///
116: /// const TTL_SECS: u64 = 30;
117: ///
118: /// impl Cache {
119: ///     fn insert(&mut self, key: CacheKey, value: Value) {
120: ///         let delay = self.expirations
121: ///             .insert(key.clone(), Duration::from_secs(TTL_SECS));
122: ///
123: ///         self.entries.insert(key, (value, delay));
124: ///     }
125: ///
126: ///     fn get(&self, key: &CacheKey) -> Option<&Value> {
127: ///         self.entries.get(key)
128: ///             .map(|&(ref v, _)| v)
129: ///     }
130: ///
131: ///     fn remove(&mut self, key: &CacheKey) {
132: ///         if let Some((_, cache_key)) = self.entries.remove(key) {
133: ///             self.expirations.remove(&cache_key);
134: ///         }
135: ///     }
136: ///
137: ///     fn poll_purge(&mut self, cx: &mut Context<'_>) -> Poll<()> {
138: ///         while let Some(entry) = ready!(self.expirations.poll_expired(cx)) {
139: ///             self.entries.remove(entry.get_ref());
140: ///         }
141: ///
142: ///         Poll::Ready(())
143: ///     }
144: /// }
145: /// ```

162: #[derive(Default)]
163: struct SlabStorage<T> {
164:     inner: Slab<Data<T>>,
165: 
166:     // A `compact` call requires a re-mapping of the `Key`s that were changed
167:     // during the `compact` call of the `slab`. Since the keys that were given out
168:     // cannot be changed retroactively we need to keep track of these re-mappings.
169:     // The keys of `key_map` correspond to the old keys that were given out and
170:     // the values to the `Key`s that were re-mapped by the `compact` call.
171:     key_map: HashMap<Key, KeyInternal>,
172: 
173:     // Index used to create new keys to hand out.
174:     next_key_index: usize,
175: 
176:     // Whether `compact` has been called, necessary in order to decide whether
177:     // to include keys in `key_map`.
178:     compact_called: bool,
179: }
180: 
181: impl<T> SlabStorage<T> {
182:     pub(crate) fn with_capacity(capacity: usize) -> SlabStorage<T> {
183:         SlabStorage {
184:             inner: Slab::with_capacity(capacity),
185:             key_map: HashMap::new(),
186:             next_key_index: 0,
187:             compact_called: false,
188:         }
189:     }
190: 
191:     // Inserts data into the inner slab and re-maps keys if necessary
192:     pub(crate) fn insert(&mut self, val: Data<T>) -> Key {
193:         let mut key = KeyInternal::new(self.inner.insert(val));
194:         let key_contained = self.key_map.contains_key(&key.into());
195: 
196:         if key_contained {
197:             // It's possible that a `compact` call creates capacity in `self.inner` in
198:             // such a way that a `self.inner.insert` call creates a `key` which was
199:             // previously given out during an `insert` call prior to the `compact` call.
200:             // If `key` is contained in `self.key_map`, we have encountered this exact situation,
201:             // We need to create a new key `key_to_give_out` and include the relation
202:             // `key_to_give_out` -> `key` in `self.key_map`.
203:             let key_to_give_out = self.create_new_key();
204:             assert!(!self.key_map.contains_key(&key_to_give_out.into()));
205:             self.key_map.insert(key_to_give_out.into(), key);
206:             key = key_to_give_out;
207:         } else if self.compact_called {
208:             // Include an identity mapping in `self.key_map` in order to allow us to
209:             // panic if a key that was handed out is removed more than once.
210:             self.key_map.insert(key.into(), key);
211:         }
212: 
213:         key.into()
214:     }
215: 
216:     // Re-map the key in case compact was previously called.
217:     // Note: Since we include identity mappings in key_map after compact was called,
218:     // we have information about all keys that were handed out. In the case in which
219:     // compact was called and we try to remove a Key that was previously removed
220:     // we can detect invalid keys if no key is found in `key_map`. This is necessary
221:     // in order to prevent situations in which a previously removed key
222:     // corresponds to a re-mapped key internally and which would then be incorrectly
223:     // removed from the slab.
224:     //
225:     // Example to illuminate this problem:
226:     //
227:     // Let's assume our `key_map` is {1 -> 2, 2 -> 1} and we call remove(1). If we
228:     // were to remove 1 again, we would not find it inside `key_map` anymore.
229:     // If we were to imply from this that no re-mapping was necessary, we would
230:     // incorrectly remove 1 from `self.slab.inner`, which corresponds to the
231:     // handed-out key 2.
232:     pub(crate) fn remove(&mut self, key: &Key) -> Data<T> {
233:         let remapped_key = if self.compact_called {
234:             match self.key_map.remove(key) {
235:                 Some(key_internal) => key_internal,
236:                 None => panic!("invalid key"),
237:             }
238:         } else {
239:             (*key).into()
240:         };
241: 
242:         self.inner.remove(remapped_key.index)
243:     }
244: 
245:     pub(crate) fn shrink_to_fit(&mut self) {
246:         self.inner.shrink_to_fit();
247:         self.key_map.shrink_to_fit();
248:     }
249: 
250:     pub(crate) fn compact(&mut self) {
251:         if !self.compact_called {
252:             for (key, _) in self.inner.iter() {
253:                 self.key_map.insert(Key::new(key), KeyInternal::new(key));
254:             }
255:         }
256: 
257:         let mut remapping = HashMap::new();
258:         self.inner.compact(|_, from, to| {
259:             remapping.insert(from, to);
260:             true
261:         });
262: 
263:         // At this point `key_map` contains a mapping for every element.
264:         for internal_key in self.key_map.values_mut() {
265:             if let Some(new_internal_key) = remapping.get(&internal_key.index) {
266:                 *internal_key = KeyInternal::new(*new_internal_key);
267:             }
268:         }
269: 
270:         if self.key_map.capacity() > 2 * self.key_map.len() {
271:             self.key_map.shrink_to_fit();
272:         }
273: 
274:         self.compact_called = true;
275:     }
276: 
277:     // Tries to re-map a `Key` that was given out to the user to its
278:     // corresponding internal key.
279:     fn remap_key(&self, key: &Key) -> Option<KeyInternal> {
280:         let key_map = &self.key_map;
281:         if self.compact_called {
282:             key_map.get(key).copied()
283:         } else {
284:             Some((*key).into())
285:         }
286:     }
287: 
288:     fn create_new_key(&mut self) -> KeyInternal {
289:         while self.key_map.contains_key(&Key::new(self.next_key_index)) {
290:             self.next_key_index = self.next_key_index.wrapping_add(1);
291:         }
292: 
293:         KeyInternal::new(self.next_key_index)
294:     }
295: 
296:     pub(crate) fn len(&self) -> usize {
297:         self.inner.len()
298:     }
299: 
300:     pub(crate) fn capacity(&self) -> usize {
301:         self.inner.capacity()
302:     }
303: 
304:     pub(crate) fn clear(&mut self) {
305:         self.inner.clear();
306:         self.key_map.clear();
307:         self.compact_called = false;
308:     }
309: 
310:     pub(crate) fn reserve(&mut self, additional: usize) {
311:         self.inner.reserve(additional);
312: 
313:         if self.compact_called {
314:             self.key_map.reserve(additional);
315:         }
316:     }
317: 
318:     pub(crate) fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
319:         self.inner.is_empty()
320:     }
321: 
322:     pub(crate) fn contains(&self, key: &Key) -> bool {
323:         let remapped_key = self.remap_key(key);
324: 
325:         match remapped_key {
326:             Some(internal_key) => self.inner.contains(internal_key.index),
327:             None => false,
328:         }
329:     }
330: }

438: impl<T> DelayQueue<T> {
439:     /// Creates a new, empty, `DelayQueue`.
440:     ///
441:     /// The queue will not allocate storage until items are inserted into it.
442:     ///
443:     /// # Examples
444:     ///
445:     /// ```rust
446:     /// # use tokio_util::time::DelayQueue;
447:     /// let delay_queue: DelayQueue<u32> = DelayQueue::new();
448:     /// ```
449:     pub fn new() -> DelayQueue<T> {
450:         DelayQueue::with_capacity(0)
451:     }
452: 
453:     /// Creates a new, empty, `DelayQueue` with the specified capacity.
454:     ///
455:     /// The queue will be able to hold at least `capacity` elements without
456:     /// reallocating. If `capacity` is 0, the queue will not allocate for
457:     /// storage.
458:     ///
459:     /// # Examples
460:     ///
461:     /// ```rust
462:     /// # use tokio_util::time::DelayQueue;
463:     /// # use std::time::Duration;
464:     ///
465:     /// # #[tokio::main]
466:     /// # async fn main() {
467:     /// let mut delay_queue = DelayQueue::with_capacity(10);
468:     ///
469:     /// // These insertions are done without further allocation
470:     /// for i in 0..10 {
471:     ///     delay_queue.insert(i, Duration::from_secs(i));
472:     /// }
473:     ///
474:     /// // This will make the queue allocate additional storage
475:     /// delay_queue.insert(11, Duration::from_secs(11));
476:     /// # }
477:     /// ```
478:     pub fn with_capacity(capacity: usize) -> DelayQueue<T> {
479:         DelayQueue {
480:             state: QueueState {
481:                 wheel: Wheel::new(),
482:                 slab: SlabStorage::with_capacity(capacity),
483:                 expired: Stack::default(),
484:                 delay: None,
485:                 wheel_now: 0,
486:                 start: Instant::now(),
487:                 waker: None,
488:             },
489:         }
490:     }
491: 
492:     /// Inserts `value` into the queue set to expire at a specific instant in
493:     /// time.
494:     ///
495:     /// This function is identical to `insert`, but takes an `Instant` instead
496:     /// of a `Duration`.
497:     ///
498:     /// `value` is stored in the queue until `when` is reached. At which point,
499:     /// `value` will be returned from [`poll_expired`]. If `when` has already been
500:     /// reached, then `value` is immediately made available to poll.
501:     ///
502:     /// The return value represents the insertion and is used as an argument to
503:     /// [`remove`] and [`reset`]. Note that [`Key`] is a token and is reused once
504:     /// `value` is removed from the queue either by calling [`poll_expired`] after
505:     /// `when` is reached or by calling [`remove`]. At this point, the caller
506:     /// must take care to not use the returned [`Key`] again as it may reference
507:     /// a different item in the queue.
508:     ///
509:     /// See [type] level documentation for more details.
510:     ///
511:     /// # Panics
512:     ///
513:     /// This function panics if `when` is too far in the future.
514:     ///
515:     /// # Examples
516:     ///
517:     /// Basic usage
518:     ///
519:     /// ```rust
520:     /// use tokio::time::{Duration, Instant};
521:     /// use tokio_util::time::DelayQueue;
522:     ///
523:     /// # #[tokio::main]
524:     /// # async fn main() {
525:     /// let mut delay_queue = DelayQueue::new();
526:     /// let key = delay_queue.insert_at(
527:     ///     "foo", Instant::now() + Duration::from_secs(5));
528:     ///
529:     /// // Remove the entry
530:     /// let item = delay_queue.remove(&key);
531:     /// assert_eq!(*item.get_ref(), "foo");
532:     /// # }
533:     /// ```
534:     ///
535:     /// [`poll_expired`]: method@Self::poll_expired
536:     /// [`remove`]: method@Self::remove
537:     /// [`reset`]: method@Self::reset
538:     /// [`Key`]: struct@Key
539:     /// [type]: #
540:     #[track_caller]
541:     pub fn insert_at(&mut self, value: T, when: Instant) -> Key {
542:         assert!(self.state.slab.len() < MAX_ENTRIES, "max entries exceeded");
543: 
544:         // Normalize the deadline. Values cannot be set to expire in the past.
545:         let when = self.normalize_deadline(when);
546: 
547:         // Insert the value in the store
548:         let key = self.state.slab.insert(Data {
549:             inner: value,
550:             when,
551:             expired: false,
552:             next: None,
553:             prev: None,
554:         });
555: 
556:         self.insert_idx(when, key);
557: 
558:         // Set a new delay if the current's deadline is later than the one of the new item
559:         let should_set_delay = if let Some(ref delay) = self.state.delay {
560:             let current_exp = self.normalize_deadline(delay.deadline());
561:             current_exp > when
562:         } else {
563:             true
564:         };
565: 
566:         if should_set_delay {
567:             if let Some(waker) = self.state.waker.take() {
568:                 waker.wake();
569:             }
570: 
571:             let delay_time = self.state.start + Duration::from_millis(when);
572:             if let Some(ref mut delay) = &mut self.state.delay {
573:                 delay.as_mut().reset(delay_time);
574:             } else {
575:                 self.state.delay = Some(Box::pin(sleep_until(delay_time)));
576:             }
577:         }
578: 
579:         key
580:     }

582:     /// Attempts to pull out the next value of the delay queue, registering the
583:     /// current task for wakeup if the value is not yet available, and returning
584:     /// `None` if the queue is exhausted.
585:     pub fn poll_expired(&mut self, cx: &mut task::Context<'_>) -> Poll<Option<Expired<T>>> {
586:         if !self
587:             .state.waker
588:             .as_ref()
589:             .map(|w| w.will_wake(cx.waker()))
590:             .unwrap_or(false)
591:         {
592:             self.state.waker = Some(cx.waker().clone());
593:         }
594: 
595:         let item = ready!(self.poll_idx(cx));
596:         Poll::Ready(item.map(|key| {
597:             let data = self.state.slab.remove(&key);
598:             debug_assert!(data.next.is_none());
599:             debug_assert!(data.prev.is_none());
600: 
601:             Expired {
602:                 key,
603:                 data: data.inner,
604:                 deadline: self.state.start + Duration::from_millis(data.when),
605:             }
606:         }))
607:     }

609:     /// Inserts `value` into the queue set to expire after the requested duration
610:     /// elapses.
611:     ///
612:     /// This function is identical to `insert_at`, but takes a `Duration`
613:     /// instead of an `Instant`.
614:     ///
615:     /// `value` is stored in the queue until `timeout` duration has
616:     /// elapsed after `insert` was called. At that point, `value` will
617:     /// be returned from [`poll_expired`]. If `timeout` is a `Duration` of
618:     /// zero, then `value` is immediately made available to poll.

770:         use crate::time::wheel::Stack;

772:         let state = &mut self.state;

774:         let prev_deadline = state
775:             .wheel
776:             .poll_at()
777:             .map(|poll_at| state.start + Duration::from_millis(poll_at));

779:         let when = state.slab[*key].when;
780:         let expired = state.slab[*key].expired;
781: 
782:         if expired {
783:             state.expired.remove(key, &mut state.slab);
784:         } else {
785:             let elapsed = state.wheel.elapsed;
786:             assert!(
787:                 elapsed <= when,
788:                 "elapsed={}; when={}",
789:                 elapsed,
790:                 when
791:             );
792: 
793:             let level_idx = crate::time::wheel::level_for(elapsed, when);
794:             let level = &mut state.wheel.levels[level_idx];
795:             let slot = slot_for(when, level_idx);
796:             level.slot[slot].remove(key, &mut state.slab);
797: 
798:             if level.slot[slot].head.is_none() {
799:                 debug_assert!(level.occupied & occupied_bit(slot) != 0);
800:                 level.occupied ^= occupied_bit(slot);
801:             }
802:         }
803: 
804:         let data = state.slab.remove(key);
805: 
806:         let next_deadline = state
807:             .wheel
808:             .poll_at()
809:             .map(|poll_at| state.start + Duration::from_millis(poll_at));

811:         if prev_deadline != next_deadline {
812:             match (next_deadline, &mut state.delay) {
813:                 (None, _) => state.delay = None,
814:                 (Some(deadline), Some(delay)) => delay.as_mut().reset(deadline),
815:                 (Some(deadline), None) => state.delay = Some(Box::pin(sleep_until(deadline))),
816:             }
817:         }

820:             key: *key,
821:             data: data.inner,
822:             deadline: state.start + Duration::from_millis(data.when),
823:         }

1179:     /// should be returned.

1183:         use self::wheel::Stack;

1185:         let expired = self.state.expired.pop(&mut self.state.slab);
1186: 
1187:         if expired.is_some() {
1188:             return Poll::Ready(expired);
1189:         }

1191:         loop {
1192:             if let Some(ref mut delay) = self.state.delay {
1193:                 if !delay.is_elapsed() {
1194:                     ready!(Pin::new(&mut *delay).poll(cx));
1195:                 }
1196: 
1197:                 let now = crate::time::ms(delay.deadline() - self.state.start, crate::time::Round::Down);
1198: 
1199:                 self.state.wheel_now = now;
1200:             }
1201: 
1202:             // We poll the wheel to get the next value out before finding the next deadline.
1203:             let wheel_idx = self.state.wheel.poll(self.state.wheel_now, &mut self.state.slab);

1205:             self.state.delay = self.next_deadline().map(|when| Box::pin(sleep_until(when)));
